text: ABSTRACT: Thiamine, a nitrogen-containing heterocyclic compound, is explored for the first time as a novel leveling agent in this study. Based on the density functional theory (DFT) calculations and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of the adsorption process of thiamine and the commonly used leveling agent JGB, the average values of the binding energies after equilibrium of thiamine and JGB are similar, which indicates that the thiamine molecules have strong bonding ability with the surface of copper and can be adsorbed tightly on the surface of copper. By cyclic voltammetry (CV) curve, thiamine was found to inhibit copper deposition and the inhibition efect was stronger than JGB. The chrono potential curve (CP) test found that the potential diference \triangle η=87>50 mV at high and low speeds of thiamine, which indicates that thiamine has the potential to be used as a leveling agent. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) testing found that thiamine inhibited copper precipitation by inhibiting the reactions of Cu ^ 2 + → Cu ^ + and Cu ^ + Cu. According to electroplating experiments, thiamine has a leveling efect on wafer electroplating and can be used as a leveling agent because the copper layer on the wafer obtained by adding it has a smoother surface compared to the copper layer obtained without adding it. It was found that wafer electroplating does not require PEG, and only adding 55 mg/L Cl −, 6 mg/L SPS, and 4 mg/L thiamine as additives can achieve a good filling efect.

text: Silicon through hole (TSV) technology, as one of the core technologies of 3D packaging, has been studied by a large number of scholars at present. 1−3 TSV is the interconnection of diferent chips and wafers by filling them with conductive metal through microvia. Compared with most metals, copper has lower resistivity and better resistance to electromigration, so the conductive metal used in TSV technology is mainly copper. 4 Direct use of the copper sulfate electroplating solution for microporous electroplating frequently results in issues, including uneven coating, flaws, and defects. Therefore, the electroplating solution often contains some additives for auxiliary electroplating, such as Cl −, accelerator, inhibitor, and leveling agent. The synergistic efect between appropriate additives can achieve better filling efect in microporous electroplating. 5−7

text: Leveling agents, like inhibitors, have the same efect on inhibiting copper deposition. 8 Currently, there is no complete consensus on the mechanism of action of leveling agents. According to reports, leveling agents can be roughly divided into two categories: quaternary ammonium cation or positively charged nitrogen-containing heterocyclic compound. 9 JGB is one of the most studied leveling agents. As shown in Figure 1, JGB is a nitrogen-containing heterocyclic compound with a positive charge. Since JGB contains N + during the electroplating process, it tends to adsorb in high charge density areas like plating raised points and microporous orifices and other locations to inhibit the copper from rising, while the depression adsorbs less leveling agent, by the inhibitory efect being less, and can therefore play the role of leveling. At present, many academics hold this belief. 10 Thiamine is a positively charged quaternary ammonium cation macromolecule, and its molecular weight (300.5) is smaller than that ofJGB (510.5), and its mass charge ratio is lower. Under the same volume, thiamine absorbs more in the high charge density area. If thiamine has the efect of inhibiting copper deposition, it may be easier to inhibit and level the efect relative to JGB.

text: Currently, there are few studies on the leveling efect of thiamine applied to electroplated copper deposition, and this study is the first study of the leveling efect of thiamine. Through electrochemical tests, quantum chemical theory calculations, molecular dynamics simulation, and other methods, we compared the properties of thiamine with those of the published leveling agent JGB and found that it has a better inhibition of copper electroplating deposition and a stronger adsorption capacity on the copper surface. In the wafer plating test, it was discovered that as compared to the plating solution without thiamine molecules, the plating solution including thiamine molecules plated the copper layer and greatly reduced the surface roughness of the wafer.

text: 2.2. Electrochemical Detection. The experiment uses a three-electrode system, with the mercury(I) sulfate electrode as the reference electrode, the Pt electrode/rotating disk Pt electrode as the working electrode, and the phosphorus copper electrode as the counter electrode. The CHI760E electro chemical workstation purchased by Shanghai Chenhua Instrument Co., Ltd. is used to test the CV, CP curves, and EIS tests. The CV test scan range is −0.8 to 0.4 V, the scanning speed is 0.01 V/s, scanning is for 3 cycles, and the second cycle is selected as the usage data. CP is the potential diference between 100 and 900 rpm under the current density of 20 mA/cm2.. The EIS test is conducted under the open circuit voltage, the frequency range is 0.01−100000 Hz, and the amplitude is 5 mV. Before the test, the electrode needs to be polished and rinsed with ultrapure water. The Virgin Makeup Solution (VMS) used is a combination of 220 g/L copper sulfate pentahydrate and 55 g/L sulfuric acid. The Cl − used in the experiment is 55 mg/L, SPS is 6 mg/L, and PEG is 220 mg/L.

text: 3.1. Quantum Chemistry Calculation and Molecular Dynamics Simulation. As shown in Figures 3−5, the optimized structure schematic, HOMO energy diagram, and LUMO energy diagram of JGB and thiamine molecules were calculated using the software Gaussian 09W and GaussView. Among them, gray white represents H atoms, gray represents C atoms, red represents O atoms, dark blue represents N atoms, and yellow represents S atoms. It can be seen from Figures 4 and 5 show that the electron cloud in JGB is concentrated on the N atom and benzene ring, and the electron cloud is relatively uniform in general, which may be parallel adsorbed on the surface of the copper layer in a large area to provide large electrodeposition steric resistance; the electron cloud of the thiamine molecule is concentrated on N^+, N, S atoms and pyrimidine ring, which indicates that N +, N, S atoms and the pyrimidine ring in the thiamine molecule are the adsorption sites of the thiamine molecule adsorbed on the surface of the copper layer, and the thiamine molecule can be adsorbed on the surface of the copper layer by providing lone pair.

text: According to molecular front orbital theory, the ability of molecules to provide and receive electrons can generally be judged according to the energy gap of the HOMO and LUMO energies. The HOMO energy is higher; the ability to provide electrons is stronger. The lower the LUMO energy, the stronger is the ability to accept electrons. Therefore, the energy gap value, Δ E, characterizes the adsorption capacity of organic molecules on metal surfaces. The lower the Δ E, the stronger the adsorption capacity. 19−21 The ΔE of thiamine molecules in this experiment is 3.1 2 \ ~eV, and the ΔE of JGB is 1.93 eV (Table 1). Although Δ E _ thiamine is greater than Δ E _ JGB, Δ E _ thiamine is less than some ΔE of leveling agents, such as ΔE tricyclazole is 6.36 eV. ^ 2 2 Therefore, the energy gap of ΔE indicates that thiamine has an adsorption capacity.

Three concentrations of thiamine were used for electroplating testing in this experiment: 10, 30, and 50 mg/L. The current density is 2ASD, and the electroplating time is 20 min. AFM testing was performed on the electroplated copper sheet to obtain the AFM test graph and obtain the average roughness (R ) and root-mean-square roughness $( R _ { \mathrm { q } } )$ corresponding to diferent solutions. It can be observed from Figure 12 and Table 3 that without the addition of thiamine, the surface $R _ { \mathrm { a } }$ of the coating is 17.8 nm and $R _ { \mathfrak { q } }$ is 23.5 nm. After adding thiamine, the roughness of the coating was significantly improved. text: Figure 13 shows the cross-sectional view of wafer micropores obtained by electroplating in diferent electroplating solutions, with the highlighted part being copper obtained by electroplating. The electroplating solutions corresponding to (a−c) did not add thiamine, and it can be seen from the figures that there are diferent defects on the copper surface. (d−f) are obtained by electroplating in a solution with the addition of thiamine. From the figures, it can be seen that after the addition of thiamine, the bulge becomes less pronounced, indicating that thiamine has a leveling efect in wafer electroplating. There are protrusions and large gaps in the (d), indicating that adding only thiamine as an additive cannot achieve good electroplating results. The copper surface in the (e) is relatively flat and free from defects, indicating that the electroplating efect is good at this time. It can be seen from (f) that although the copper surface is flat, there are voids in the copper layer. Overall, it was found that under this aspect ratio of the wafer substrate, only 55 mg/L Cl −, 6 mg/L SPS, and 4 mg/L thiamine needed to be added to obtain better filling.

text: In this experiment, through theoretical calculations and molecular dynamics simulations, the diference between thiamine and the leveling agent JGB was compared, and it was determined that the adsorption capacity and adsorption behavior of thiamine on the copper surface would inhibit the deposition of copper better. By conducting CV and CP tests on leveling agent JGB and new leveling agent thiamine, the study shows that the CV oxidation peak area obtained after adding thiamine is smaller than that of adding JGB, and the potential diference of thiamine at high and low rotational speeds \triangle η=87~ mV > 5 0 ~ mV, suggesting its potential as a leveling agent. Through EIS testing, it was found that the addition of thiamine not only inhibited the Cu ^ 2 + → Cu ^ + reaction but also suppressed the Cu ^ + → Cu reaction. Through electroplating experiments, it was found that thiamine has a leveling efect on copper deposition and can be applied to wafer microhole electroplating. Moreover, in wafer electroplating, it was found that without adding inhibitors, only 55 mg/L Cl −, 6 mg/L SPS, and 4 mg/L thiamine as leveling agents can achieve a good filling efect.
